lessons.title: Nouns
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A noun names a person, place, thing or idea.
  • Common nouns name a class — elephant, animal, house.
  • Proper nouns name a particular person or place — Ravi River, Indus River.
  • Collective nouns name a group taken together — crowd, flock, class, furniture.
  • Abstract nouns name a quality or state — truth, honesty, health, happiness.

Solved Exercises

1. The crowd is very big.
Crowd — Collective Noun. It is the name of a group of people taken together.

2. The elephant is an intelligent animal.
Elephant — Common Noun; animal — Common Noun. Both are names of a class of living beings, not of any particular one.

3. The Ravi River is one of the five tributaries of the Indus River.
Ravi River — Proper Noun; tributaries — Common Noun; Indus River — Proper Noun. The names of particular rivers are proper nouns, while tributaries is a common noun.

4. The shepherd took the flock of sheep to the field.
Shepherd — Common Noun; flock — Collective Noun; sheep — Common Noun; field — Common Noun. A flock is a group of sheep taken together.

5. I bought furniture for my new house.
Furniture — Collective Noun; house — Common Noun. Furniture is the name of a collection of household articles taken together.

6. Always speak the truth.
Truth — Abstract Noun. It is the name of a quality which cannot be seen or touched.

7. He gave me a bunch of grapes.
Bunch — Collective Noun; grapes — Common Noun. A bunch is a group of grapes taken together.

8. The class is studying grammar.
Class — Collective Noun; grammar — Abstract Noun. A class is a group of students, and grammar is the name of a subject.

9. We all love honesty.
Honesty — Abstract Noun. It is the name of a quality which cannot be seen or touched.

10. Without health, there is no happiness.
Health — Abstract Noun; happiness — Abstract Noun. Both are names of states or qualities, not of persons or things.

mcqs.why: The notes classify crowd as a Collective Noun because it is the name of a group of people taken together.

mcqs.why: Truth is an Abstract Noun in the notes because it names a quality which cannot be seen or touched.

mcqs.why: Bunch is a Collective Noun because, as the notes explain, a bunch is a group of grapes taken together.

lessons.title: Pronouns
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A pronoun stands in place of a noun.
  • Use he, she, we, they as the subject of a sentence.
  • Use him, her, us, them as the object of a verb or preposition.
  • Use his, her, its, their before a noun to show possession.

Solved Exercises

1. Munir is a good boy. He always listens to his teacher.
He, his

2. Amir and Salman are twin brothers. They take the same bag to school.
They

3. Murad and I are very good friends. We have known each other since childhood.
We

4. The mangoes are very sour. Where did you buy them?
them?

5. I love watching Tom and Jerry cartoons. They remind me of my childhood days.
They remind

6. I bought this book for my sister. We often read it together.
We

7. This is Sara. Do you know her?
her?

8. There are many windows here. But all of them are jammed.
them

9. The army has reached its destination.
its

10. My aunt and uncle live in Multan. We often visit them.
We, them.

mcqs.why: The notes state his, her, its, their are used before a noun to show possession, as his is used before teacher.

mcqs.why: They is used in the notes as the subject of remind for Tom and Jerry cartoons, so the subject form is required.

mcqs.why: Her is correct because the notes use her after know, as the object of a verb, following him, her, us, them for objects.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'There are many windows here. But all of ___ are jammed.'
mcqs.why: The solved exercise uses them for the windows in 'all of them are jammed', matching the notes exactly.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'The army has reached ___ destination.'
mcqs.why: Its is correct because the notes use its before the noun destination to show possession by the army.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'My aunt and uncle live in Multan. We often visit ___.'
mcqs.why: Them is the object pronoun in the notes for aunt and uncle after the verb visit, while We is the subject.

lessons.title: Adverbs
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • An adverb modifies a verb, an adjective or another adverb.
  • Adverbs of manner tell how — soundly, valiantly.
  • Adverbs of time tell when — soon, already.
  • Adverbs of degree tell how much — too, very, rather.
  • Adverbs of frequency tell how often — always.

Solved Exercises

1. The boy is too careless.
The adverb is "too". It modifies the adjective "careless" and shows the degree of carelessness.

2. The winds are very strong.
The adverb is "very". It modifies the adjective "strong" and shows the degree of strength.

3. The baby slept soundly.
The adverb is "soundly". It modifies the verb "slept" and shows the manner of sleeping.

4. The soldiers fought the war valiantly.
The adverb is "valiantly". It modifies the verb "fought" and shows the manner of fighting.

5. Jaffar always tries his best.
The adverb is "always". It modifies the verb "tries" and shows the frequency of the action.

6. Surely you are mistaken.
The adverb is "Surely". It modifies the whole sentence and shows the certainty of the speaker.

7. The movie is to end soon.
The adverb is "soon". It modifies the verb "is to end" and shows the time of the action.

8. Your friend messaged again.
The adverb is "again". It modifies the verb "messaged" and shows that the action happened once more.

9. I had already done my homework.
The adverb is "already". It modifies the verb "had done" and shows that the action was completed before.

10. I was rather busy.
The adverb is "rather". It modifies the adjective "busy" and shows the degree of busyness.

mcqs.why: The notes say the adverb is too, it modifies the adjective careless and shows the degree of carelessness.

mcqs.why: Very modifies the adjective strong and, according to the notes, shows the degree of strength.

mcqs.why: The notes state soundly modifies the verb slept and shows the manner of sleeping.

mcqs.why: Valiantly modifies the verb fought and shows the manner of fighting, so it is an adverb of manner.

mcqs.why: The notes say always modifies the verb tries and shows the frequency of the action.

mcqs.why: Soon modifies the verb is to end and shows the time of the action, making it an adverb of time.

mcqs.why: The notes say rather modifies the adjective busy and shows the degree of busyness.

lessons.title: Verbs
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A verb tells what a person or thing does, or what happens.
  • The verb must agree with its subject in number and person.
  • Use the past form for a finished action — caught, went, ran.

Solved Exercises

1. Rabia runs a mile every day.
runs

2. The dogs bark all night.
bark

3. The cat caught the snake.
caught

4. We play in the park in the evenings.
play

6. Aqib wants to be a police officer when he grows up.

7. Maheen ran back to her mother.
ran

8. Khalid walks very fast.

9. You can come with us.
come

10. They went to a picnic together yesterday.
went

lessons.title: Adjectives
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • An adjective describes a noun or pronoun.
  • It tells what kind, how many, or which one — homeless, sly, little.
  • Some adjectives describe degree — pretty sour.

Solved Exercises

1. The homeless beggar hasn't eaten for days.
The adjective is "homeless". It describes the noun "beggar".

2. The fox is a sly animal.
The adjective is "sly". It describes the noun "animal".

3. Mary had a little lamb.
The adjective is "little". It describes the noun "lamb".

4. The selfish giant didn't allow the children to enter his garden.
The adjective is "selfish". It describes the noun "giant".

5. The foolish dog barked at its reflection and lost its food.
The adjective is "foolish". It describes the noun "dog".

6. The family didn't have enough food for the winter.
The adjective is "enough". It describes the quantity of the noun "food".

7. The girl is a state-level boxer.
The adjective is "state-level". It describes the noun "boxer".

8. The brave army marched through the streets.
The adjective is "brave". It describes the noun "army".

9. I had no idea that such a fantastic place existed anywhere.
The adjective is "fantastic". It describes the noun "place".

10. Some oranges are pretty sour.
The adjective is "pretty". It is used here to describe the degree of sourness of the oranges.

lessons.title: Prepositions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A preposition shows the relation of a noun or pronoun to another word.
  • Common prepositions — for, among, in, to, on, at, of.
  • Learn the fixed pairs — faithful to, fond of, born on.

Solved Exercises

1. This shop doesn't have the toys I was looking for.
for.

2. The teacher divided the sweets among all the children.

3. Babar did not fare well in his examination.

6. The boy at the store is quite young.

7. Anam was born on the 2nd October.
on

8. Rashid is fond of muffins.
of

9. The dog jumped on the sofa.
on

10. Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall.
on

lessons.title: Punctuation
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Use a comma to join two short clauses — “We had a great time in France, the kids really enjoyed it.”
  • Use a question mark at the end of a direct question.
  • Use an apostrophe for possession — the girl’s father — and in Murphy’s Law.
  • Use inverted commas for words actually spoken.

Solved Exercises

1. We had a great time in France the kids really enjoyed it
We had a great time in France, the kids really enjoyed it.

2. Some people work best in the mornings others do better in the evenings
Some people work best in the mornings, others do better in the evenings.

3. What are you doing next weekend
What are you doing next weekend?

4. Mother had to go into hospital she had heart problems
Mother had to go into hospital, she had heart problems.

5. Did you understand why I was upset
Did you understand why I was upset?

6. It is a fine idea let us hope that it is going to work
It is a fine idea, let us hope that it is going to work.

7. We will be arriving on Monday morning at least I think so
We will be arriving on Monday morning, at least I think so.

8. A textbook can be a wall between a teacher and a class
A textbook can be a wall between a teacher and a class.

9. The girls father sat in a corner
The girl's father sat in a corner.

10. In the words of Murphys Law Anything that can go wrong will go wrong
In the words of Murphy's Law, "Anything that can go wrong will go wrong."

lessons.title: Tenses
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Present Indefinite — a habit or fact: Dawood drinks coffee every morning.
  • Past Indefinite — a finished action: The boy got up late.
  • Present Continuous — an action in progress: The team is playing.
  • Present Perfect — an action just finished or with present result: The baby has eaten all the chips.
  • Present Perfect Continuous — an action continuing up to now: has been sleeping for three hours.
  • Past Continuous — an action in progress in the past: Samia was going to school.
  • Past Perfect — the earlier of two past actions: Pervez had done his homework when her parents came back.
  • Future Indefinite — an action yet to happen: I will move to Sialkot soon.

Solved Exercises

1. Dawood drinks coffee every morning.
Present Indefinite Tense (Simple Present Tense).

2. The boy got up late and missed the bus.
Past Indefinite Tense (Simple Past Tense).

3. The team is playing very well.
Present Continuous Tense.

4. The school will be closed for winter break.
Future Indefinite Tense (Simple Future Tense, passive form).

5. Lubna graduated from this college last year.
Past Indefinite Tense (Simple Past Tense).

6. The baby has eaten all the chips.
Present Perfect Tense.

7. Have you read Pride and Prejudice?
Present Perfect Tense (interrogative form).

8. The train has just left the station.
Present Perfect Tense.

9. The sick child has been sleeping for three hours.
Present Perfect Continuous Tense.

10. They have known each other for a long time.
Present Perfect Tense.

11. Samia was going to school.
Past Continuous Tense.

12. When I went there, Bashir was playing video games.
Past Continuous Tense (with Past Indefinite Tense in the main clause).

13. The workers have been working on the building for a long time.
Present Perfect Continuous Tense.

14. Pervez had done his homework when her parents came back.
Past Perfect Tense (with Past Indefinite Tense in the main clause).

15. I will move to Sialkot soon.
Future Indefinite Tense (Simple Future Tense).

lessons.title: Correction of Common Errors
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • People and cattle are already plural — never peoples or cattles.
  • Sheep has the same form in singular and plural.
  • After a modal (could, would) and after to, use the base form of the verb.
  • Importance takes the preposition of.
  • The verb must agree with its subject — children were, man has.
  • Keep the tense the same in one sentence — I saw Raheem when I was on the flight.

Solved Exercises

1. Many peoples attended the funeral of the great man.
Many people attended the funeral of the great man. (People is already the plural of person.)

2. The shepherd took the cattles to the field.
The shepherd took the cattle to the field. (Cattle is already plural.)

3. Sitara could not understands what the teacher was saying.
Sitara could not understand what the teacher was saying. (After a modal, the base form of the verb is used.)

4. Do you know the importance for clean water?
Do you know the importance of clean water? (Importance takes the preposition of.)

5. Laugh is the best medicines.
Laughter is the best medicine. (Laughter is the noun subject; medicine is uncountable.)

6. The flock of sheeps blocked the road.
The flock of sheep blocked the road. (Sheep has the same form in singular and plural.)

7. The children was playing in the giant's garden.
The children were playing in the giant's garden. (Children is plural, so the verb is were.)

8. The children decided to surprises Miss Holmes on teacher's day.
The children decided to surprise Miss Holmes on Teachers' Day. (After to, the base form of the verb is used.)

9. I saw Raheem when I'm on the flight.
I saw Raheem when I was on the flight. (The past tense must be used to match saw.)

10. Man have depended on nature for a long time.
Man has depended on nature for a long time. (Man as a collective subject takes the singular verb has.)

options: Many peoples attended the funeral of the great man.
Many people attended the funeral of the great man.
Many person attended the funeral of the great man.
Many peoples attend the funeral of the great man.
mcqs.why: The notes explain people is already the plural of person, so the corrected sentence uses 'people', never 'peoples'.

mcqs.why: The notes state cattle is already plural, so the corrected sentence is 'The shepherd took the cattle to the field.'

mcqs.why: After a modal such as could, the base form of the verb is used, so 'understands' is corrected to 'understand'.

mcqs.why: The notes state importance takes the preposition of, giving the corrected sentence 'the importance of clean water'.

mcqs.why: The notes correct it to 'Laughter is the best medicine' because laughter is the noun subject and medicine is uncountable.

options: The flock of sheep blocked the road.

mcqs.why: The notes state sheep has the same form in singular and plural, so 'sheeps' is corrected to 'sheep'.

mcqs.q: What is the correct verb in 'The children ___ playing in the giant's garden'?
mcqs.why: The verb must agree with its subject: children is plural, so the notes correct 'was' to 'were'.

mcqs.q: What is the correction of 'The children decided to surprises Miss Holmes on teacher's day'?
options: The children decided to surprised Miss Holmes on teacher's day.
The children decided to surprising Miss Holmes on Teachers' Day.
The children decided to surprises Miss Holmes on Teachers' Day.
The children decided to surprise Miss Holmes on Teachers' Day.
mcqs.why: After to, the base form of the verb is used, so the notes give 'to surprise' and the corrected form 'Teachers' Day'.

mcqs.q: What is the correction of 'I saw Raheem when I'm on the flight'?
options: I saw Raheem when I am on the flight.

mcqs.why: The tense must stay the same in one sentence: the past tense 'was' is used to match 'saw', as the notes state.

lessons.title: Types of Sentences
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Declarative — states a fact. Interrogative — asks a question.
  • Imperative — gives an order or request. Exclamatory — expresses strong feeling.
  • By structure: Simple — one main clause; Complex — one main clause and a subordinate clause; Compound-Complex — two main clauses and a subordinate clause.

Solved Exercises

1. Please shut the windows and doors.
Imperative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

2. Do you like chocolate pastries?
Interrogative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

3. Where are you going?
Interrogative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

4. Such a beautiful place!
Exclamatory sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

5. Go and try this new flavour.
Imperative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

6. Today is Monday.
Declarative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

7. Please clean your cupboard today.
Imperative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

8. Turn off all the lights and fans when you leave the room.
Imperative sentence (function); Complex sentence (structure, with the subordinate clause when you leave the room).

9. May I come in?
Interrogative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

10. How would you like your coffee?
Interrogative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

11. I love reading storybooks.
Declarative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

12. The Earth revolves around the Sun.
Declarative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

13. Alas!
We have lost the trophy. Exclamatory sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

14. Hurray!
We have won the competition. Exclamatory sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

15. He lives in a big city.
Declarative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure).

16. As soon as the bell rang, the students rushed out.
Declarative sentence (function); Complex sentence (structure, with the subordinate clause as soon as the bell rang).

17. He looked at his father and smiled.
Declarative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure, with a compound predicate).

18. Aslam and Anwar had their dinner and went for a walk.
Declarative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure, with a compound subject and predicate).

19. The little boy started crying when he could not find his toy.
Declarative sentence (function); Complex sentence (structure, with the subordinate clause when he could not find his toy).

20. Akbar forgot his friend's birthday, so he sent him a card when he finally remembered.
Declarative sentence (function); Compound-Complex sentence (structure, with two main clauses and one subordinate clause).

21. While playing cricket, the ball thrown by my friend hit a man crossing the road.
Declarative sentence (function); Simple sentence (structure, with participial phrases).

mcqs.q: According to the notes, a declarative sentence does what?
mcqs.why: The key points define the four functions: Declarative states a fact, as in 'Today is Monday.'

mcqs.q: By structure, a complex sentence consists of what?
options: One main clause and a subordinate clause
Two main clauses and a subordinate clause
mcqs.why: The key points define a Complex sentence as one main clause and a subordinate clause.

mcqs.q: By structure, a compound-complex sentence consists of what?
options: Two main clauses and a subordinate clause
One main clause and a subordinate clause
mcqs.why: The key points define a Compound-Complex sentence as two main clauses and a subordinate clause.

mcqs.q: Why is 'Turn off all the lights and fans when you leave the room' a complex sentence by structure?
options: Because it has the subordinate clause 'when you leave the room'
mcqs.why: The notes classify it as Complex in structure, with the subordinate clause 'when you leave the room'.

mcqs.why: The notes classify it as Complex in structure, with the subordinate clause 'as soon as the bell rang'.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Grammar Exercise 6 (Direct and Indirect Speech)

lessons.title: Pick the Correct Indirect Speech
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • In indirect speech the tense moves one step back — have baked becomes had baked.
  • A question in indirect speech uses the statement order — where the weapons were.
  • An exclamation becomes exclaimed with wonder / sorrow and the tense moves back.
  • Note: the source gives the four options for each sentence without marking the correct one, so no answer key is given here.
  • Note: in Question 3 the options (b) and (c) are printed exactly alike in the source.

Solved Exercises

1. She said, "I have baked a cake."
(a) She said that she baked a cake.
(b) She said that she had baked a cake.
(c) She said that I baked a cake.
(d) She said that she had bake a cake.

2. Ali said, "What a beautiful rainbow it is!"
(a) Ali exclaimed wonderfully that it was a beautiful rainbow.
(b) Ali exclaimed with wonder that the rainbow was beautiful.
(c) Ali exclaimed with wonder that the rainbow is beautiful.
(d) Ali exclaimed with wonder that it was a beautiful rainbow.

3. She said, "They did not invite her for the dinner."
(a) She said that they did not invite her for the dinner.
(b) She said that they had not invited her for the dinner.
(c) She said that they had not invited her for the dinner.
(d) She said that we had not invited her for the dinner.

4. The policeman said, "Where are the weapons?"
(a) The policeman questioned where was the weapons.
(b) The policeman questioned where are the weapons.
(c) The policeman questioned where were the weapons.
(d) The policeman questioned where the weapons were.

5. The man said, "Ah! I am ruined."
(a) The man cried that he was in ruined.
(b) The man exclaimed in grief that he was ruin.
(c) The man said that Ah, he is ruined.
(d) The man exclaimed with sorrow that he was ruined.

mcqs.q: Pick the correct indirect speech: She said, 'I have baked a cake.'
options: She said that she baked a cake.
She said that she had baked a cake.
She said that I baked a cake.
She said that she had bake a cake.
mcqs.why: In indirect speech the tense moves one step back, so 'have baked' becomes 'had baked' and 'I' becomes 'she'.

mcqs.q: Pick the correct indirect speech: Ali said, 'What a beautiful rainbow it is!'
options: Ali exclaimed wonderfully that it was a beautiful rainbow.
Ali exclaimed with wonder that the rainbow is beautiful.
Ali said that what a beautiful rainbow it was.
Ali exclaimed with wonder that it was a beautiful rainbow.
mcqs.why: An exclamation becomes 'exclaimed with wonder' and the tense moves back, so 'it is' becomes 'it was' in the notes' conversion.

mcqs.q: Pick the correct indirect speech: She said, 'They did not invite her for the dinner.'
options: She said that they did not invite her for the dinner.
She said that they had not invited her for the dinner.
She said that we had not invited her for the dinner.
She said that they had not invite her for the dinner.
mcqs.why: The past action moves one step back in indirect speech, so 'did not invite' becomes 'had not invited' while 'they' stays unchanged.

mcqs.q: Pick the correct indirect speech: The policeman said, 'Where are the weapons?'
options: The policeman questioned where was the weapons.
The policeman questioned where are the weapons.
The policeman questioned where were the weapons.
The policeman questioned where the weapons were.
mcqs.why: A question in indirect speech uses statement order, so the notes give 'where the weapons were', not the question order 'where were the weapons'.

mcqs.q: Pick the correct indirect speech: The man said, 'Ah! I am ruined.'
options: The man exclaimed with sorrow that he was ruined.
The man cried that he was in ruined.
The man said that Ah, he is ruined.
The man exclaimed in grief that he was ruin.
mcqs.why: The notes convert this exclamation as 'exclaimed with sorrow' and move 'am' back to 'was', giving 'he was ruined'.

mcqs.q: In the sentence 'I have baked a cake', what does 'have baked' become in indirect speech?
mcqs.why: The key point in the notes is that the tense moves one step back in indirect speech, so 'have baked' becomes 'had baked'.

mcqs.q: Which word order is used for a question changed into indirect speech?
mcqs.why: The notes state that a question in indirect speech uses the statement order, as in 'where the weapons were'.

options: Ali said with wonder that it was a beautiful rainbow.
Ali cried with wonder that it was a beautiful rainbow.
Ali exclaimed with wonder that it was a beautiful rainbow.
Ali asked with wonder that it was a beautiful rainbow.
mcqs.why: The notes use 'exclaimed with wonder' for this exclamation and move the tense back from 'is' to 'was'.

mcqs.q: In 'She said that she had baked a cake', the pronoun 'I' from the direct speech has become:
mcqs.why: The speaker in the direct sentence is 'she', so 'I have baked' is reported as 'she had baked' in the notes' conversion.

mcqs.why: The tense moves one step back in indirect speech, so 'I am ruined' becomes 'he was ruined' in the notes.

lessons.title: Change into Indirect Speech
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Now becomes then; present becomes past in the reported clause.
  • A request becomes requested me to + the base verb.
  • An exclamation of sorrow becomes exclaimed with sorrow that.

Solved Exercises

1. Junaid said, 'I am very busy now.'
Junaid said that he was very busy then.

2. He said, 'They have not watered the plants.'
He said that they had not watered the plants.

3. 'Alas, there is nobody to support me,' said John.
John exclaimed with sorrow that there was nobody to support him.

4. 'German is easy to learn,' she said.
She said that German was easy to learn.

5. He said to me, 'Open the door, please.'
He requested me to open the door.

6. 'It is too late to go out,' said Ali.
Ali said that it was too late to go out.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: Junaid said, 'I am very busy now.'
options: Junaid said that he was very busy then.
Junaid said that he is very busy now.
Junaid said that I was very busy then.
Junaid said that he was very busy now.
mcqs.why: The notes give 'Junaid said that he was very busy then': 'am' becomes 'was' and 'now' becomes 'then'.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: He said, 'They have not watered the plants.'
options: He said that they have not watered the plants.
He said that they has not watered the plants.
He said that they had not watered the plants.
He said that they did water the plants.
mcqs.why: The present form moves back in the reported clause, so 'have not watered' becomes 'had not watered' as in the notes.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: 'Alas, there is nobody to support me,' said John.
options: John said that alas, there is nobody to support me.
John exclaimed with sorrow that there was nobody to support him.
John exclaimed with sorrow that there is nobody to support me.
John requested that there was nobody to support him.
mcqs.why: The notes convert this exclamation of sorrow as 'exclaimed with sorrow that there was nobody to support him', with 'is' back to 'was' and 'me' to 'him'.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: 'German is easy to learn,' she said.
options: She said that German is easy to learn.
She said that German was being easy to learn.
She said that German has been easy to learn.
She said that German was easy to learn.
mcqs.why: The notes give 'She said that German was easy to learn', because the present 'is' becomes the past 'was' in the reported clause.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, 'Open the door, please.'
options: He requested me to open the door.
He requested me to opened the door.
He said to me to please open the door now.
He ordered me that I open the door.
mcqs.why: A request becomes 'requested me to' plus the base verb, so the notes give 'He requested me to open the door'.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: 'It is too late to go out,' said Ali.
options: Ali said that it is too late to go out.
Ali said that it was too late to go out.
Ali said that it has been too late to go out.
Ali said that it were too late to go out.
mcqs.why: The notes give 'Ali said that it was too late to go out', moving the present 'is' back to the past 'was'.

mcqs.q: In indirect speech, the word 'now' in Junaid's sentence changes to:
mcqs.why: The key point in the notes is that 'now' becomes 'then', as shown in 'he was very busy then'.

mcqs.q: A request such as 'Open the door, please' is reported with 'requested me to' followed by:
mcqs.why: The notes state that a request becomes 'requested me to' plus the base verb, giving 'to open the door'.

mcqs.q: In the reported sentence 'German was easy to learn', the direct speech verb was:
mcqs.why: The direct sentence is 'German is easy to learn'; the present 'is' becomes 'was' when it is reported, as the notes show.

mcqs.q: The word 'Alas' at the start of John's sentence shows that it is reported as an exclamation of:
mcqs.why: The notes convert 'Alas, there is nobody to support me' with 'exclaimed with sorrow', because 'Alas' expresses sorrow.

Cell means a small room or the smallest unit of life. Sentence: The prisoner was kept in a cell. Sell means to give something for money. Sentence: He wants to sell his car.

lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Write the moral first, then a brief summary of the story.
  • Keep the summary short — the main events and the lesson only.

Solved Exercises

1. “Honesty is the Best Policy”
Moral: Honesty is the best policy. An old king gave each of his three sons a seed to plant. The two elder sons cheated by planting other seeds when theirs did not grow, but the youngest son honestly showed his empty pot because the seeds given were dead and useless. The king made the honest son the next king, because honesty is the most important quality of a king.

2. “A Friend in Need is a Friend Indeed”
Moral: A friend in need is a friend indeed. Two friends walking in a forest promised never to leave each other in need. When a bear appeared, one climbed a tree and left the other, who lay flat like a dead body, since a bear does not eat a dead body. The bear went away, and the friend on the ground said the bear had whispered that a friend in need is a friend indeed. The false friend felt ashamed and apologized.

3. “Union is Strength”
Moral: United we stand, divided we fall. An old farmer gave his quarrelling sons a bundle of sticks which none of them could break. When the bundle was untied, each stick broke easily. The father taught them that if they live together in peace, none can harm them, but if they are divided, they will lose.

4. “The Mouse and the Lion”
Moral: Love and kindness are never wasted. A lion spared a tiny mouse who begged for mercy and promised to repay him. A few days later the lion was caught in a hunter's net, and the little mouse gnawed the net with her sharp teeth until the lion was free. Thereafter, the lion and the mouse became good friends.

5. “The Foolish Stag”
Morals: All that glitters is not gold; Appearances are often deceptive; Pride hath a fall. A stag was proud of his beautiful antlers and hated his thin, ugly legs. When hounds chased him, his despised legs carried him far away, but his beautiful antlers got caught in a thick bush, and the hounds tore him to pieces.

6. “The King and the Spider”
Morals: Perseverance paves the way for success; Try, try again until you succeed; No pain, no gain. King Robert Bruce of Scotland had lost six battles and was hiding in a cave. He watched a spider fail six times to spin its thread across the cave, and succeed on the seventh attempt. Inspired, he gathered his army once more and won back his kingdom.

lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Write the moral first, then a brief summary of the story.

Solved Exercises

7. “Greed is a Curse”
Moral: Greed is a curse. Three friends found a bag full of gold on a picnic. Two of them planned to kill the third who went to bring food, so they could have a bigger share. The third friend poisoned the food to kill the other two and keep all the gold himself. The two killed him, ate the poisoned food, and died too. The gold was still there, but it was of no use to them.

8. “As You Sow, So Shall You Reap”
Morals: As you sow, so shall you reap; Tit for tat. A jackal rode on a camel's back across a river and then howled after a meal, bringing the field owner who thrashed the camel. On the way back, the camel dived into the deep river, saying that bathing after a hearty meal was his habit, and the jackal drowned.

9. “Look Before You Leap”
Morals: Look before you leap; Haste makes waste. A hunter left his baby with his faithful dog. A wolf entered and the dog killed it to save the baby. The hunter returned, saw the dog's blood-stained snout, thought the dog had killed his child, and shot the dog. Then he found his child safe and a dead wolf beside him, and realized his mistake, but crying over spilt milk was of no use.

10. “The Thief and His Mother”
Moral: Nip the evil in the bud. A boy stole a book from a classmate, and his mother encouraged him instead of scolding him. He went on stealing bigger things until he was caught red-handed and sentenced to long imprisonment. On his way to jail he bit his mother's ear and said that if she had slapped him after the first theft, he would not have gone to jail and would have lived like a decent person.

11. “The Hare and the Tortoise”
Moral: Slow and steady wins the race. A proud hare laughed at the slow tortoise and accepted a race. The hare ran far ahead, then slept under a tree, confident that the tortoise would take ages to reach him. The slow and steady tortoise kept moving without rest, passed the sleeping hare, and won the race.

12. “The Crow and the Pitcher”
Morals: Necessity is the mother of invention; A good use of our wits may help us out; Little by little does the trick. A thirsty crow found a pitcher with very little water at the bottom, out of reach of his beak. He dropped pebbles into the pitcher one by one, and the water rose a little higher with each pebble, until he could drink and save his life.

13. “A Stitch in Time Saves Nine”
Moral: A stitch in time saves nine. A merchant ignored a stableman's advice to fix a loose nail in his horse's shoe, saying one nail makes no difference. The shoe came off, the horse limped, night fell, and robbers whipped him and grabbed his cash. His delay in a small repair cost him his horse and his money.

14. “A Rolling Stone Gathers No Moss”
Moral: A rolling stone gathers no moss. In a war between birds and animals, the bat sided with whoever seemed to be winning, claiming to be a bird with the birds and an animal with the animals. When the animals won, both sides turned the bat out. Since then, the bat has become a symbol of duplicity, showing its face neither to animals nor to birds, and coming out only in the dark.

15. “An Arab and His Camel”
Moral: Give him an inch, and he will take an ell. On a cold desert night, an Arab allowed his camel to put only its head, then its neck, then its hump inside the tent. Step by step the camel pushed its whole body in, until the Arab woke up outside in the cold while the camel slept peacefully inside. The Arab said that one should not be too kind to others, or one will lose all one has.

16. “The Bee and the Dove”
Morals: One good turn deserves another; Kindness never goes unrewarded. A dove dropped a leaf near a bee drowning in a river, and the bee dried her wings and flew away safely. Later, when a hunter aimed at the dove, the bee stung the hunter, his shot missed, and the dove flew away. Thus the bee paid the debt of the dove's favour.

17. “The Little Fish”
Morals: A bird in hand is worth two in the bush; A small gain is worth more than a large promise. A fisherman caught a very small fish which begged to be put back, promising that it would grow much bigger and could be caught again later. The fisherman replied that it might never be caught again, and kept the small fish, which his wife cooked and they ate with relish.

18. “The Hen that Laid Golden Eggs”
Morals: Haste makes waste; Greed is a curse; It is useless to cry over spilt milk; Contentment is a great blessing. A cloth merchant owned a hen that laid one golden egg every day. Not satisfied, he killed the hen to get all the eggs at once, but found nothing inside but blood. He was grieved because now he would not get even a single egg.

lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Write the moral first, then a brief summary of the story.

Solved Exercises

19. “The Wolf and the Lamb”
Moral: Might is right. A wolf drinking upstream accused a lamb downstream of muddying his water. The lamb replied that the water flows from the wolf to him, not from him to the wolf. The wolf then accused the lamb of abusing him last year, but the lamb said he was not born last year and was only six months old. The wolf said it must have been his father or mother, and tore the lamb to pieces and devoured it.

20. “King Midas and the Golden Touch”
Moral: Don't be greedy in life, be happy with what you have. King Midas wished that everything he touched should turn into gold. His food, drink, and even his beloved daughter Marigold turned into gold, and he was horrified. He begged the fairy to take back his wish, bathed in a pond and sprinkled the water on all he had touched, and his daughter came back to life. Thereafter, he promised to stop being greedy.

21. “The Boy Who Cried Wolf”
Moral: A liar will not be believed, even when he speaks the truth. A shepherd boy twice cried "Wolf! Wolf!" for fun, and the villagers ran up the hill only to find no wolf. When a real wolf came and he cried out loudly, the villagers thought he was fooling them again and did not come. The wolf scattered the flock, and an old man told him that nobody believes a liar, even when he is telling the truth.

22. “A Wise Counting”
Moral: A witty answer will serve its purpose. Emperor Akbar asked his courtiers how many crows there were in the city. Birbal replied at once: "There are fifty thousand five hundred and eighty-nine crows, my lord." When Akbar asked how he could be so sure, Birbal said that if more were found, it meant some had come to visit their relatives, and if fewer, some had gone to visit relatives elsewhere. Akbar was pleased with Birbal's wit.

23. “The Blue Jackal”
Morals: Be true to yourself and don't pretend to be someone you are not; Every action has an opposite reaction; Tit for tat. A jackal fell into a tub of blue dye and, looking completely blue, claimed to the jungle animals that God had sent him to be their king. He ruled them and even threw out the other jackals. One day the banned jackals howled, and the blue jackal howled out of habit too, so the animals identified him as a jackal and unmasked his true identity.

lessons.title: Model Letters
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A letter starts with the address and date, then Dear…, then the body, then Yours sincerely / affectionately / obediently.
  • Keep it short, polite and to the point — one purpose in each letter.

Solved Exercises

1. Write a letter inviting a friend to a birthday party.
House No. 12, Street No. 4, Lahore. 15th March 2026. Dear Ali, I hope you are in good health. I am writing to invite you to my birthday party, which will be held at my house on Sunday, 22nd March, at 6 p.m. All our common friends will also be there, and we shall enjoy music, games and dinner together. Please do come and make the occasion happy for me. I shall wait for you eagerly. Yours sincerely, Ahmed.

2. Write a letter calling a friend for a trip or a holiday.
House No. 12, Street No. 4, Lahore. 15th March 2026. Dear Ali, I hope you are fine. As the summer vacation is about to begin, I have planned a trip to Murree with my family, and I wish you to join us. We shall leave on 5th June and return after a week. The weather there is pleasant, and we shall visit the Mall Road, Patriata and Ayubia together. Please take permission from your parents and let me know soon. Yours sincerely, Ahmed.

3. Write a letter apologizing to someone for the mistakes you have done.
House No. 12, Street No. 4, Lahore. 15th March 2026. Dear Uncle, I am writing this letter with a heavy heart to apologize for my rude behaviour yesterday. I spoke harshly without thinking, and I have realized my mistake. I am truly sorry for hurting your feelings. I promise that I shall never repeat such behaviour again. I hope you will forgive me and treat me as before. Yours obediently, Ahmed.

4. Write a letter congratulating a friend on his success or achievement.
House No. 12, Street No. 4, Lahore. 15th March 2026. Dear Ali, I was overjoyed to hear that you have stood first in the annual examination. Please accept my heartiest congratulations on this splendid success. Your hard work and regularity have borne fruit, and your parents and teachers must be very proud of you. I wish you still greater success in the future. Keep it up. Yours sincerely, Ahmed.

5. Write a letter just to ask for the well-being of a person.
House No. 12, Street No. 4, Lahore. 15th March 2026. Dear Grandmother, I hope you are in the best of health. It has been a long time since I heard from you, so I am writing to ask about your well-being. How is your health now? Are you taking your medicine regularly? We all miss you very much and pray for your long life. Please write to me about yourself in detail. Yours affectionately, Ahmed.

6. Write a letter of invitation to attend a marriage.
House No. 12, Street No. 4, Lahore. 15th March 2026. Dear Ali, I am glad to inform you that the marriage ceremony of my elder sister will be held on 10th April at our house. The Barat will arrive in the evening, followed by dinner. I cordially invite you and your family to attend the ceremony and bless the couple. Your presence will add to our joy. Please do come. Yours sincerely, Ahmed.

7. Write a letter seeking help from someone.
House No. 12, Street No. 4, Lahore. 15th March 2026. Dear Uncle, I hope you are well. I am writing to seek your help in a difficulty. My father has fallen ill and is admitted to hospital, and I need some money for his treatment. I shall be grateful if you could lend me ten thousand rupees for a month. I promise to return the amount as soon as possible. I hope you will not disappoint me. Yours obediently, Ahmed.

8. Write a letter informing about someone's demise in family or friends.
House No. 12, Street No. 4, Lahore. 15th March 2026. Dear Ali, It is with deep sorrow that I inform you of the sad demise of my grandfather, who passed away yesterday after a brief illness. His funeral prayer will be offered today at 4 p.m. in the Jamia Masjid near our house. We are all in deep grief at this irreparable loss. Please pray for the departed soul and attend the funeral if possible. Yours sincerely, Ahmed.

mcqs.q: According to the Key Points, what is the correct order of parts in a letter?
options: Body, then Dear, then address and date
Address and date, then Dear, then the body, then Yours sincerely / affectionately / obediently
Subject, then Respected Sir, then the request
Dear, then Yours obediently, then the body
mcqs.why: The Key Points state a letter starts with the address and date, then Dear, then the body, then Yours sincerely / affectionately / obediently.

mcqs.why: The model letter invites Ali to a birthday party at Ahmed's house on Sunday, 22nd March, at 6 p.m. with music, games and dinner.

options: To Murree, visiting Mall Road, Patriata and Ayubia

mcqs.why: The well-being letter to his grandmother ends with 'Yours affectionately, Ahmed' as shown in the model in the notes.

mcqs.why: The notes state his father is ill in hospital and Ahmed asks his uncle to lend ten thousand rupees for a month for the treatment.

mcqs.why: The model letter informs Ali that the marriage ceremony of Ahmed's elder sister will be held on 10th April, with the Barat arriving in the evening.

options: His uncle, after a long illness

mcqs.why: The notes say Ahmed informs Ali with deep sorrow of the sad demise of his grandfather, who passed away yesterday after a brief illness.

options: House No. 10, Street No. 2, Lahore, 10th April 2026

lessons.title: Model Applications
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • An application starts with To, The Principal…, then the Subject, then Respected Sir, then the request, then Yours obediently with name and roll number.
  • State the reason clearly and ask for one thing only.

Solved Exercises

1. Write an application requesting for a college leaving certificate.
To, The Principal, Government College, Lahore. Subject: Request for College Leaving Certificate. Respected Sir, I beg to state that I have passed my Intermediate examination from your college this year. I have taken admission to the University, where I am required to submit my college leaving certificate. I shall be grateful if you kindly issue me the certificate at your earliest convenience. Yours obediently, Ahmed, Roll No. 24.

2. Write an application requesting for leave to attend a seminar.
To, The Principal, Government College, Lahore. Subject: Request for Leave to Attend a Seminar. Respected Sir, I beg to state that I have been selected to present a paper in a seminar on science education, to be held in Islamabad on 20th and 21st March. I request you to kindly grant me leave for two days, from 20th to 21st March, so that I may attend the seminar. I shall be grateful to you. Yours obediently, Ahmed, Roll No. 24.

3. Write an application seeking permission for organizing a sports gala.
To, The Principal, Government College, Lahore. Subject: Request for Permission to Organize a Sports Gala. Respected Sir, I beg to state that the students of our college wish to organize a sports gala on the college ground on 5th April. Cricket, football, badminton and race competitions will be held, and prizes will be awarded to the winners. We request you to kindly grant us permission and provide the ground for the occasion. Yours obediently, Ahmed, Sports Secretary.

4. Write an application requesting to arrange make-up classes for English.
To, The Principal, Government College, Lahore. Subject: Request for Make-up Classes for English. Respected Sir, I beg to state that our English course could not be completed because the teacher remained on leave for two weeks. The examination is near, and the students are worried about the incomplete syllabus. We request you to kindly arrange make-up classes for English in the afternoon so that the course may be completed in time. Yours obediently, Ahmed, Class Representative.

5. Write an application requesting the principal for a month's medical leave.
To, The Principal, Government College, Lahore. Subject: Request for One Month's Medical Leave. Respected Sir, I beg to state that I have been suffering from typhoid, and the doctor has advised me complete bed rest for one month. I am enclosing the medical certificate with this application. I request you to kindly grant me medical leave for one month, from 1st to 30th April. I shall be grateful to you. Yours obediently, Ahmed, Roll No. 24.

6. Write an application requesting the principal for condoning short of lectures.
To, The Principal, Government College, Lahore. Subject: Request for Condoning Shortage of Lectures. Respected Sir, I beg to state that my attendance has fallen short of the required percentage because I remained ill for a long period during this term. I have now recovered and am attending classes regularly. I request you to kindly condone my shortage of lectures and allow me to appear in the examination. I shall be grateful to you. Yours obediently, Ahmed, Roll No. 24.

7. Write an application requesting the principal for one week's leave for your sister's marriage.
To, The Principal, Government College, Lahore. Subject: Request for One Week's Leave for Sister's Marriage. Respected Sir, I beg to state that the marriage ceremony of my elder sister will be held on 10th April, and I have to make arrangements and attend the functions. I request you to kindly grant me leave for one week, from 8th to 14th April. I shall cover the missed lessons with the help of my classmates. Yours obediently, Ahmed, Roll No. 24.

8. Write an application requesting the principal for seeking apology for misconduct.
To, The Principal, Government College, Lahore. Subject: Apology for Misconduct. Respected Sir, I beg to state that I behaved rudely with my teacher yesterday in the classroom, for which I am deeply ashamed. I have realized my mistake and I sincerely apologize for my misconduct. I promise that I shall never repeat such behaviour in future and shall always respect my teachers. I request you to kindly forgive me. Yours obediently, Ahmed, Roll No. 24.

9. Write an application requesting the principal for changing your section or subjects.
To, The Principal, Government College, Lahore. Subject: Request for Change of Section/Subjects. Respected Sir, I beg to state that I am a student of Section A, but my close friends are in Section B, and I face difficulty in group study. Moreover, I wish to change my optional subject from Economics to Computer Science, as I am more interested in it. I request you to kindly allow me to change my section and subject. I shall be grateful to you. Yours obediently, Ahmed, Roll No. 24.

mcqs.q: According to the Key Points, what is the correct order of parts in an application?
options: Respected Sir, then To The Principal, then the Subject
To The Principal, then the Subject, then Respected Sir, then the request, then Yours obediently with name and roll number
Address and date, then Dear, then the body
Subject, then Yours sincerely, then the request
mcqs.why: The Key Points state an application starts with To, The Principal, then the Subject, then Respected Sir, then the request, then Yours obediently with name and roll number.

mcqs.why: The notes say he has passed Intermediate this year and taken admission to the University, where he is required to submit his college leaving certificate.

mcqs.why: The model application requests medical leave for one month, from 1st to 30th April, as clearly stated in the notes.

mcqs.q: Why does Ahmed request the principal to condone his shortage of lectures?
options: His attendance fell short because he remained ill for a long period during the term
He was attending his sister's marriage functions
He was presenting a paper at a seminar
He was organizing the sports gala
mcqs.why: The notes say his attendance fell short of the required percentage because he remained ill for a long period, and he now attends regularly.

mcqs.why: The notes state the marriage is on 10th April and Ahmed requests leave for one week, from 8th to 14th April, to make arrangements and attend functions.

options: From Section B to Section A, and from Computer Science to Economics
From Section A to Section B, and from Economics to Computer Science

lessons.title: Sample Paragraphs — Spring Season to A Hot Day in Summer
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A paragraph is one short piece of writing on one topic.
  • Begin with the main idea, add a few supporting lines, and close with one concluding line.

Solved Exercises

1. Spring Season
Spring is the season of mists and mellow fruitfulness. The days get longer and nights shorter, the temperatures are milder, and the flowers bloom. There is a gentle wind that blows making the atmosphere wonderful. Spring is the season that brings new life to trees, plants and flowers. During spring one can hear the buzzing of bees, chirping of birds and can see the colourful butterflies sitting over sweet-scented flowers. This season brings happiness, motivation, and positivity to all people and brings sunshine into the lives of people. It is a season of pleasant weather free from the scorching heat, the cold bites or dodgy rains. It is therefore crowned as the king of all the seasons.

2. My Best Friend
Having a true friend is a precious gift and a divine blessing of Allah. I am lucky to have many true friends. Among all, the one who is my best friend is Ali. He has been with me since class one. He is very friendly and has a kind nature. His good sense of humour makes him popular among everyone. He is one of the best students in our class. He is punctual and he always comes to college on time. Both of us share the love for reading and enjoy reading books history the most. We also exchange books with each other and discuss them in our free time. We study and play together. Whenever I feel sad or depressed, he is there to help me cheer up my mood. In short, the bond that I share with my best friend is the most prized possession I have. A best friend is indeed a precious gem and I am fortunate to have found that gem in my life.

3. My Favourite Personality
Everyone has one favourite person in his life that he can always rely on. I am fortunate to have one such person in my life who is none other than my father. He has always been a source of motivation and inspiration in my life. I have seen him working hard since my childhood to provide us with the best of everything. He has always been caring and loving. He is the one who has helped me become a better person. The quality of my father that I admire the most is that he has always kept a very safe and friendly environment at home. We are never scared of talking or discussing any issue with him. He would always listen to us and give us his best advice. In fact, he is my best friend who is not only loving and caring but he is always there for me, no matter who he is. He is the best one in the world.

4. My Hobby
Life would be dull if one did not have some good hobby. A good hobby keeps us active and creative. It kills monotony and makes a person happy. Reading is what I do in my spare time. This hobby of mine not only brings me pleasure but also increases my knowledge. It improves my vocabulary and writing skills. I have a great collection of books ranging from history and politics to novels, short stories and poetry. I am also a member of various libraries. Though I read all sorts of books, I particularly take more interest in books related to history. It gives me insight into the happenings around the world and provides a link to the past. Through reading history books, I have learnt a lot about the evolution of the cultures and traditions of many countries. Reading is a good brain exercise.

5. A Hot Day in Summer
It was a sultry and scorching summer's day. The sun glowed red hot, emitting sizzling bright rays. There was quietness all over. Not a single person could be seen outside. The roads and streets almost presented a deserted look. Fans and cold drinks gave no relief. Everybody was perspiring from head to toe. People preferred to stay indoors. It was so hot that things were at such a standstill that not even a leaf stirred anywhere. The plants and trees presented a withered look. It appeared as if the wind had conspired not to blow. Everyone wanted to get rid of this heat. Such hot summer days make people uncomfortable.

lessons.title: Sample Paragraphs — Mobile Phone to Poverty
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A paragraph is one short piece of writing on one topic.
  • Begin with the main idea, add a few supporting lines, and close with one concluding line.

Solved Exercises

6. Mobile Phone
Technological advancement has made the life of modern man easier and more convenient. The major breakthrough is in the field of communication. From simple telephones to cellular phones, the distances have further reduced and the world has come closer. It is a very useful device that works without wire and is portable also. It can make and receive calls over a radio frequency link and connects people in no time. It provides a platform for communication with an individual's family and friends, no matter where they are. Mobile phones provide various facilities like cameras, internet, e-banking and much more. With mobile phones, one never feels lonely or bored.

7. Corruption
Corruption is the root cause of a country's weak political, social as well as economic system. It is a curse for society. It hampers the growth of the nation and is a great deterrent to the progress and prosperity of a country. Factors which encourage systematic corruption include conflicting incentives, discretionary powers, monopolistic powers, lack of transparency, low pay and a culture of impunity. Thus, it hurts the growth of each individual in the country. It is a great evil of a society which needs to be eliminated at every cost. It is a poison that has penetrated the minds of individuals nowadays. Strict measures should be taken by the government to ensure a corruption-free country.

8. Terrorism
Terrorism is an act that aims at creating fear among the people by illegal means. It is a threat to humanity. It includes persons or groups spreading violence, riot, kidnapping, bombing, etc. It makes people suffer traumatic stress disorders, anxiety and major depression. It is generally believed that poverty, inequality, and poor economic conditions are among the root causes of terrorism. It jeopardizes the happiness and peace of the people in a country. The purpose of terrorism is to achieve political or ideological aims by spreading unrest and lawlessness. Terrorism is an act of cowardice.

9. Smog
Smog is air pollution that reduces visibility. The term smog was first introduced in the early 1900s to describe a mixture of smoke and fog. Smog is usually caused by the combustion of coal, wood and other solid fuels. Smog is very common in industrial areas and it remains a familiar sight in cities, particularly in the winter. Smog inhalation irritates our airways and increases our risk of serious heart and lung diseases. It is due to these health hazards that cities monitor smog levels. On a high ozone-alert day, eyes and throat may burn, resulting in cough and wheeze. It is of utmost importance that people should take positive steps to control smog so that they can live in a healthy environment.

10. Poverty
Poverty is about not having enough money to meet basic needs including food, clothing and shelter. The World Bank Organization describes poverty in this way: "Poverty is hunger." Poverty is a source of problems and pain in human life. Owing to poverty people live their entire life in the absence of essential commodities. A poverty-stricken person can neither meet his needs nor that of his family. Poverty always acts as a barrier on the path of happiness. Poverty limits access to educational and employment opportunities which further contribute to income inequalities. This menace can be eliminated through equity, education, and resilience.

lessons.title: Essay Outlines — Internet to Advantages and Disadvantages of Cell Phones
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • An essay outline has three parts — Thesis (the main idea), Body (the points in order), Conclusion (the closing thought).
  • Learn the outline point by point, then write the essay in your own words.

Solved Exercises

1. Internet
Thesis: The internet is a worldwide spread computer network, the only means of exchanging data through computer networking, which has swept the world off its feet with its vast usage. Body: (1) It has enabled the growth of society both positively and negatively, diluting some moral values but helping in economy, culture, politics and religion. (2) Communication platforms like Facebook, WhatsApp and email have shortened distances and introduced video calls. (3) Education has been made easy through websites like Google, and online learning is gaining accreditation worldwide. (4) The negative side: obsession with virtual identities at the expense of real selves. Conclusion: One should not let the tech environment eat up one's whole real existence; netizens should remember that excess of everything is bad, and only limits ensure freedom.

2. Traffic Problems in Big Cities
Thesis: Travelling has become more comfortable and quicker due to the boom in the automobile industry, but it has caused many traffic problems, and the traffic problem in a big city has gone beyond proportion. Body: (1) Traffic congestion makes a city's life miserable; jams last for hours, people miss offices and schools, patients miss medical aid, and passengers feel frustrated and angry. (2) Causes: unchecked population growth and influx of villagers, narrow and uneven roads, and people not educated enough to follow traffic rules. (3) Measures: urbanize the villages and discourage migration, educate people to follow traffic rules, widen and maintain roads, and discourage protocol culture and reserved roads for V.I.Ps. Conclusion: Traffic jams are a daily occurrence, but the given measures can help reduce traffic congestion in big cities.

3. A Visit to a Zoo
Thesis: Gone are the days when zoo trips used to be the most thrilling spot children loved to visit, but for a person who has never visited a zoo, such a trip can be a cherishing experience and offers many learning opportunities. Body: (1) The Lahore Zoo visit on a Sunday with family; tickets at 11.30 a.m.; water birds on a blue lake, a white duck, and a birds' enclosure with sparrows, pigeons, eagles and parrots. (2) Wild animals: lions, tigers, leopards and tigresses, whose roars terrorized the children; the tiger's den, elephants and bears. (3) A garden with stags and deer, monkeys and baboons jumping for bananas, deserted-looking polar bears, and a tank of crocodiles, cobras and pythons. Conclusion: A simple touch taught a lot and gave an incredible experience; a trip to the zoo will never fail to bring out the inner child in you.

4. Village Life
Thesis: A village reflects a picture of regional, cultural and social customs, very different from an urban area; life is simple and pure, with mud houses, narrow paths and unpaved roads. Body: (1) Pakistan is predominantly agricultural; the majority live in villages, enjoying matchless scenic beauty, lush green fields, tall trees and blossoming flowers. (2) Village life is calm, peaceful, free of noise pollution and the rush of traffic; villagers are simple, sincere, industrious, hospitable and generous, enjoying mutual cooperation. (3) The occupation of most villagers is agriculture, with hard work from early morning; government offices and factories are rare, though a few artisans like carpenters and blacksmiths work there. (4) Problems: village life is a mixed blessing, devoid of basic amenities, lagging in education, modern cultivation and facilities, though villagers entertain themselves with folk dances, fairs and music like Mahiyas and Tappas. Conclusion: More than seventy per cent of our people live in villages, but very little attention is given to uplifting them; without solid measures for the improvement of village life, Pakistan cannot make progress by leaps and bounds.

5. My Last Day at College
Thesis: College life is one of the best periods of one's life, a life of freedom, friendship and intellectual growth, and that is why the last day at college brings tears to the eyes and grief to the heart. Body: (1) The writer reached college on a sunny April morning, feeling that everything would become a memory of the past. (2) The teachers were emotional too; the students sought guidance on future plans and cheered themselves with jokes. (3) The cafeteria, the centre of all activities, welcomed them with cold drinks and snacks free of cost. (4) A farewell dinner at the Boarding House, organized by the talented first-year juniors, with singers among teachers and students, and the Principal and Vice Principal wishing a bright future. Conclusion: Finally the festivities came to an end; that day was indeed a memorable event of life, and weighed down with a heavy heart, the writer returned home along the lonely road.

6. Advantages and Disadvantages of Cell Phones
Thesis: The mobile phone is a significant technological advancement, small, portable and affordable, which has greatly benefitted the human race, but it also has negative aspects. Body: (1) Advantages: communication with anyone anywhere in the world; information through a click, with 55% of adults keeping a cell phone to access information; education flourished through learning applications; entertainment without going to cinemas. (2) Disadvantages: it creates distance between parents, friends and relatives; distraction through video games and social media; a health hazard for the young generation; dependence, wasting precious time, money and energy; cybercrime and data-stealing applications. Conclusion: Through mobile phones the world has become one big family, but mind can be an excellent slave and a poor master; cell phones are a means of communication and should be used in a way that one may not become a slave to them.

lessons.title: Essay Outlines — Festivals to Examinations
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • An essay outline has three parts — Thesis (the main idea), Body (the points in order), Conclusion (the closing thought).
  • Learn the outline point by point, then write the essay in your own words.

Solved Exercises

7. Festivals
Thesis: Festivals are celebrations that make a nation honour its values and culture, and a nation celebrates different festivals to promote its culture by sharing the reasons of past events. Body: (1) Pakistani people celebrate cultural festivals with great zeal; some festivals are nation-wide and others within certain communities, all with complete unity. (2) Pakistan is the land of diverse ethnicities with deeply-rooted cultural and religious values. (3) Religious festivals: Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Adha and Eid Milad-un-Nabi, celebrated with religious passion. (4) National and cultural festivals: Independence Day, Defence Day, Resolution Day, Mela Chiraghan, Shandur Polo Festival, Quaid's Day and Iqbal's Day. (5) Minorities' festivals: Christmas, Easter, Guru Nanak's Birthday and Holi. Conclusion: All these festivities are organized to celebrate special events, the government announces public holidays on some of them, and they are celebrated with great zeal and zest by the communities of our beloved motherland.

8. A Rainy Day
Thesis: Rainy days are expected during the rainy season and are an absolute joy for men, women and especially children; rain after a long hot scorching summer is a welcoming relief. Body: (1) The sparkling clear shower pacifies souls and rejuvenates spirits; paper boats, pearl-like raindrops on trees and flowers, and chirping birds delight the eyes. (2) For children, rainy days are a sudden break from busy schedules; they run about splashing water, stretch arms out of car windows, and smile as raindrops drip from their palms. (3) Schoolchildren draw smiling faces in smoke on window glass; poets capture natural dreams in metaphors; the tinkling sound of rain on tin roofs infuses new spirit into exhausted souls. Conclusion: Mother nature brings us back to her lap where we forget the worries of modern life; rainy days become harbingers of a new life, and every dark cloud has a silver lining which renews hope and motivates us.

9. My Favourite Personality
Thesis: My favourite personality is Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, a man of great courage and determination whose charismatic personality stimulates enthusiasm, courage and energy in people and unites them as a nation. Body: (1) Born in Karachi on 25th December 1876, in a well-off merchant's family; his father Poonjah Jinnah was conscious of his son's education; he observed discipline which pointed to his bright future. (2) After matriculation he went to England, studied law in Lincoln's Inn, became a barrister, and started law practice in Karachi, becoming a distinguished lawyer. (3) He joined the Indian National Congress, then the Muslim League and became its leader; he united the Muslims on a single platform and fought for their rights despite failing health. (4) In 1940 he declared the Lahore Resolution demanding a separate state, making people realize that Muslims and Hindus are different in traditions and religion and cannot live together in a single state. Conclusion: Quaid-e-Azam united and led an oppressed nation to a state where they could live an independent and free life; owing to his love, honesty and truthfulness he became the most charismatic leader of Muslim history, who said: "There is no power on the Earth that can undo Pakistan."

10. Terrorism
Thesis: Terrorism is an act which aims at creating fear among people by illegal means; it is a threat to humanity and an act of cowardice, often construed as a well thought-out extreme form of violence. Body: (1) It includes persons or groups spreading violence, riots, burglaries, kidnapping, fighting and bombing. (2) Since 9/11, Pakistan has been at the epicenter of both terrorism and the war against it, gaining a negative reputation, though terrorism has nothing to do with religion and extremists use religion as an alibi. (3) Effects: lives of all and sundry destroyed, millions of goods destroyed, thousands of lives lost, families torn apart, people losing hope, and a cycle of uncertainty which only begets violence. (4) The dilemma: terrorists are common people like us, victims of social injustices or brainwashed by extremist groups, trained to act violently against their own society. Conclusion: Terrorism has spread across the world, contaminating innocent minds and stripping them of their sense of security; to reduce the regime of terror, a tight security arrangement should be made on the orders of the government.

11. A Road Accident
Thesis: Every now and then we hear of accidents, common sights in large cities, which kill and cripple people for life; the reason for most accidents is violation of traffic rules, and public transport buses are the worst offenders. Body: (1) Last week the writer witnessed a terrifying accident: a city bus at great speed lost control, collided head-on with another vehicle, crashed through barriers, and smashed into an iron railing and boundary wall. (2) A passerby was crushed under the bus and died instantly; a few passengers lost their lives and some were injured seriously, while the driver of the other vehicle survived miraculously. (3) People gathered, helped victims out through windows, and the police and Rescue 1122 arrived in time; the driver and conductor fled at once. (4) The police took the bus papers to identify the driver and owner; witnesses said the driver was driving rashly while attempting to overtake another bus. Conclusion: It was late night when the writer came home, but the memory of that accident haunted him for many days to come.

12. Examinations
Thesis: No nation can progress without education, and a well-reformed system of examination is necessary for better education, but unfortunately our system of examination is replete with faults. Body: (1) The current system only tests the memory of students and does not test their knowledge, understanding and comprehension, so students learn through cramming and rote learning. (2) The method of evaluation does not do justice: examiners mark differently, some strict and some lenient, making assessment personal and inaccurate, and subjective questions cannot be awarded exact marks. (3) Malpractices: corrupt invigilators take money and help students cheat, papers are leaked, and students bribe examiners. (4) Examinations are held in the scorching heat of summer with power outages, and short academic terms mean courses cannot be completed. (5) Reforms: more emphasis on critical thinking to minimize rote learning, examinations in the spring season for pleasant weather, longer academic years, question papers testing knowledge and insight, and motivation through prizes and scholarships. Conclusion: These reforms will enable students to focus on grasping concepts rather than learning them by heart, and will muster up their motivation to perform well.
