lessons.title: Essay Outlines — Education System of Pakistan to Patriotism
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • An essay outline has three parts — Thesis (the main idea), Body (the points in order), Conclusion (the closing thought).
  • Learn the outline point by point, then write the essay in your own words.

Solved Exercises

13. Education System of Pakistan
Thesis: Education is the process of acquiring knowledge, developing skills, getting training and learning moral values, necessary for a stable life, self-independence and self-confidence, and its main goal is to develop a high sense of responsibility, social integrity and selfless service to the nation. Body: (1) The system lacks uniformity, divided into private and government sectors, which promotes discrimination; the elite class is attracted by the private sector while government schools are of low quality due to lack of accountability and inadequate budget. (2) Lack of qualified and trained staff is a main reason for the poor system. (3) Parental participation is crucial, but without it, policy implementation remains a far cry. (4) Causes of suffering: lack of budget, lack of implementation of policies, poor physical facilities, political interference, old and outdated curriculum, unavailability of science and computer laboratories, and old teaching methods still prevalent. (5) The media seems paralysed by political influence and does not highlight corrupt practices; officials eye their own interests instead of bringing visible changes. Conclusion: In short, there is a need of the hour to take radical measures to reform the ailing state education system, so that more intellectual literates can be produced, who will bring us to limelight and lead us to the glory we deserve as a nation.

14. Atomic Energy
Thesis: During the Second World War, America fought against Japan, and both countries tried hard to make a weapon that could vanquish the enemy completely; Einstein had already presented his theory of relativity, and finally the Americans succeeded in making an atomic bomb, the first of its nature. Body: (1) The bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki caused hellacious massacre and destruction, turning thousands of people into ashes in an instant, showing how dangerous atomic energy could be for war purposes. (2) Scientists have worked on using this technology for peaceful and constructive ends; the splitting of atoms creates an infinite amount of energy which can cause unlimited destruction if left unchecked, but if harnessed properly it can solve energy crises efficiently. (3) Research found that a few grams of the desired element could satisfy the electricity demands of thousands of villages. (4) Compared with other energy types, nuclear power is environmentally friendly: it generates clean energy by bombarding uranium with neutrons instead of burning fossil fuels, produces no carbon dioxide emissions, and its waste has a fairly low level of radioactivity. Conclusion: More than seven countries have atomic plants working for the betterment of humankind; it is a highly emphasized fact that atomic energy should only be used for productive sources and not for destructive ends.

15. Pollution
Thesis: Pollution is the main factor which affects our lives badly on the earth; there are several types such as noise, water, air and land pollution, and it is hazardous to life, changing and damaging habitats and affecting other species. Body: (1) Air pollution is the deadliest type, caused by unwanted particles suspended in the air; leading causes are smoke from cars, factories and CFCs, which destroy the ozone layer that blocks bad rays from the sun; carbon dioxide envelops the atmosphere, raising temperature day by day, melting ice and causing floods. (2) Water pollution: humans throw garbage and waste into clean water, factories dispose of unwanted chemicals, drinkable water is reducing, and oil spillage kills thousands of marine lives. (3) Land pollution: people do not throw garbage into trashcans but onto the land, and waste disposal companies do not dispose of it at proper sites. Conclusion: Pollution is not only harmful but a very serious threat; to fight this menace, vigorous efforts should be put in, anti-pollution law should be strictly implemented, sewage and factory waste should be dumped properly, and public education and awareness of the relationship between climate change and human health is the key to dealing with these problems more effectively.

16. The Dignity of Labour
Thesis: Nobody in this world can survive independently, as we are all social animals who work in collaboration with one another; people believe that professions fetching good money are respectable, but all jobs and professions are respectable provided they are permissible and done honestly. Body: (1) Islam puts great emphasis on the dignity of labour; we come across many jobs where people work as helpers in houses, electricians, plumbers, sewerage workers, gardeners and road cleaners, all contributing to the welfare of society and no less honourable than doctors, teachers or engineers. (2) Treating them with utmost respect is everyone's duty, yet some people treat labourers harshly and inhumanely, and some do not pay their wages just in time. (3) Everyone should understand that all professions are equally respectable and should be regarded in high esteem; if these people stop doing their jobs, life will become a living hell. (4) Remedies: labourers should be dealt with dignity and treated equally; discrimination against labourers should be discouraged by spreading awareness; campaigns should convey that labourers should be equally respected; strict punishment and legal action should be taken against those who insult or harass them or do not pay them timely. Conclusion: The dignity of labour should not be compromised by any means because it is a sin against humanity; labourers should be given due respect, and we ought to pay respect to all and sundry, no matter what one does for one's living.

17. Uses of Science
Thesis: Gone are the days when people believed that the planet Earth is stationary and flat and the Sun revolves around it; then science came and rejected all these theories, and people started to discover new things, new continents, new routes and new worlds. Body: (1) Life before science was very dull and dark, without electricity, gas, telephone, internet, vehicles or television, and people lived in fear and without adventure. (2) Scientists brought revolutions through wonderful discoveries in every walk of life; new theories were tested and turned into laws, and inventions kept getting better with time. (3) The first computer occupied a lot of space and was operated by many people with limited functions; with time computers became smaller and smaller, and now laptops can be carried anywhere easily with all the functions a person can ask for. (4) People are no longer afraid of superstitions like black cats, broken mirrors, spilled milk, the sound of scissors and the number thirteen, because science has proved that all superstitions are baseless and have no sound reasoning or logic behind them. Conclusion: In short, science is the greatest collective endeavour; it ensures a longer and healthier life, monitors our health, provides medicines to cure diseases, alleviates our aches and pains, helps us provide clean water for our basic needs including food, and invigorates us by sports, music, entertainment and the latest communication technology; last but not least, science nourishes our spirit.

18. Patriotism
Thesis: Patriotism is the feeling of love and devotion to one's country, an inborn and pure feeling which surpasses all things in one's life; a true patriot knows the actual worth of his country and understands the sacrifices one ought to make for it. Body: (1) Everyone ought to be a patriot because the country takes care of him like his own mother, nurtures him at every stage, and provides a home, food and air to breathe in. (2) Pakistan is our dear country, and a true patriot should know how it came into being and what hardships the leaders bore; Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah worked day and night for independence from the British, while the Hindus were the British favourites and Muslims were at a disadvantage, yet he remained firm and worked hard. (3) A separate homeland was attained at the cost of severe atrocities during migration; thousands were brutally murdered but refrained from yielding. (4) Soon after independence, the due financial share of Pakistan was not handed over, unfair adjustments were made so Pakistan could fail, and a war was imposed to destroy Pakistan once and for all, but true patriots offered their lives and saved the country many times. Conclusion: Loyalty and love are the two characteristics every patriot should possess; a person not fighting for the cause of the country cannot be called a patriot, and loving one's nation is integral to one's personality; at the time of distress, we should be ready to stand by our homeland, to work for it, and even to sacrifice our lives for it, if the need be.

lessons.title: Essay Outlines — Beggary to Hostel Life
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • An essay outline has three parts — Thesis (the main idea), Body (the points in order), Conclusion (the closing thought).
  • Learn the outline point by point, then write the essay in your own words.

Solved Exercises

19. Beggary
Thesis: Begging is the act of asking favour, including money, clothes and food, for free with no intent of reciprocation; it is as old as human history, and people with no option for survival have often been seen supporting themselves through it, mostly starting when a person is in desperate need. Body: (1) Causes: various financial, social and biological factors, the most important being poverty, unemployment, and the conception of beggary as a lucrative source of income; in developed countries economies are stable and inflation is low, so very few beg, while in under-developed countries low wages, ever-increasing inflation and lack of jobs make lives extremely difficult. (2) Types: some beggars are in desperate need with no alternative; some just beg for the sake of it as their profession; needy people often give up begging when helped, but some beggars function under beggar mafias which recruit people, govern rings, and control the beggars, who are found involved in supply of drugs, loot, plunder, murder and other crimes. (3) Professional beggars know the art of winning sympathy, use emotional and religious blackmail, deceive people by portraying themselves as helpless, and the drowsy, sleepy infants in the laps of their so-called mothers are often found drugged; Islam is strictly against professional beggary and prohibits giving alms to such people. Conclusion: Beggary is loathsome whether done by profession or out of dire need; awareness should be spread against it, and it needs to be ended by the people and government through strict laws and proper planning; being poor is not a crime, but fulfilling one's needs through illegal means instead of hard work is a huge crime, and elimination of this single blight will nip many evils in the bud.

20. Why I Love My Country
Thesis: Love for one's country is an inborn phenomenon, a natural and pure feeling which surpasses all things in one's life; Pakistan is my country, emancipated from the shackles of the British on 14th August 1947, rich in culture and tradition, with diversity of race, languages, food and places. Body: (1) I love my country because it is my motherland; I was born and brought up here, and she takes care of me like my own mother, nurturing me at every stage and providing a home, food and air to breathe in. (2) It is the land of lofty mountains: the Hindu Kush, Himalayas and Karakoram ranges with majestic, sublime and boundless beauty; Pakistan is home to the world's second-highest peak K2, occasionally known as the King of Mountains and the Mountaineers Mountain, a source of great pride. (3) It is blessed with fascinating lakes like Saif-ul-Malook, Satpara, Ansoo and Attabad Lake; the Arabian Sea touches its southern part, and rivers like the Ravi, Satluj, Chenab, Jhelum, Indus and Kabul irrigate its fertile and rich agricultural lands. (4) Technological advancements have reached new heights: Pakistan is one of the few powerful countries with atomic technology attained in the 1980s, advanced tactical warfare machinery including long-range ballistic missiles, next-generation fighter aircraft and loaded warships, and new technological fields and hubs. Conclusion: In the end, Pakistan is blessed with all the treasures and is by no means inferior to any other country; on account of these reasons, among too many to mention, I love my motherland from the bottom of my heart.

21. My Aim in Life
Thesis: An aimless life is directionless; aims and goals are very important for a person's life, and without a serious goal, life is useless and makes people dull; to develop personal utility, it is crucial to have a clear aim in mind, and striving hard for an aim makes a person capable and productive. Body: (1) Different people dream differently: some wish to be doctors or engineers, some to be architects, teachers or developers; my aim in life is to be a soldier in the army, because there I can directly serve my nation, and the mission of our army is to defend the nation from known and unknown factors. (2) Countless heroes are present in our army and are role models: Naik Saif Ali Janjua, Captain Muhammad Sarwar, Major Tufail Muhammad, Major Raja Aziz Bhatti, Pilot Officer Rashid Minhas, Major Shabbir Sharif, Sowar Muhammad Hussain, Major Muhammad Akram, Lance Naik Muhammad Mahfuz, Havildar Lalak Jan and Captain Karnal Sher Khan are an epitome of pride and inspiration, besides thousands of unheard heroes still working to protect our country. (3) There is a hard procedure for selection: multiple trials including a preliminary knowledge test, an initial medical test, a physical test and an interview, followed by psychological and performance tests to test aptitude. (4) The writer knows his strengths and weaknesses and has been working day and night to overcome shortcomings, and will apply after the intermediate examination to secure a place in the army and become a proud defender of the country. Conclusion: One must dream big, sky is the limit; the choices we make can bring differences in our lives and in the lives of those for whom we want to make a difference; it requires courage, strong will power, determination, consistent efforts, patience, persistence and perseverance to fulfil one's dream, and challenges, problems and setbacks are bound to come, but once we have taken a decision, we need to keep striving till the end.

22. A Journey by Train
Thesis: Travelling and nature are the great masters as they teach us through experiences; travelling is one of the exciting ways to experience and observe nature, and trains are a fascinating means of transportation whose greatest benefit is that we make many observations. Body: (1) The writer had travelled on an airplane and a ship, but his most desired wish was to travel by train; one day he had to go to Rawalpindi for a test and chose the train after a moment's hesitation, pre-booking an A.C. sleeper ticket a week before. (2) He reached the station at 7 o'clock, but the train was delayed due to technical issues and finally arrived at 9:30 a.m. with a roaring sound; the conductor guided him politely to a neat, clean, air-conditioned cabin with berths, shared with only one other man. (3) From the window he saw trees, crop fields, working farmers and the scenery of nature quickly sliding past, stopping at every station, until the train at last reached his destination. Conclusion: Many great writers and philosophers have written inspirational quotes related to trains; the train travel symbolises the ups and downs of life, and just like the invention of the train has brought a great transformation to world transportation, it can bring a noticeable transformation to the minds of travellers who love nature by observing their surroundings.

23. A Visit to a Hill Station
Thesis: Visiting a hill station in the summer can be full of fun and excitement; it is the best way to get rid of the scorching heat of the city, and its pleasant weather and temperature are helpful in maintaining health. Body: (1) After papers were over, the writer needed a break from the day-to-day grind; on a friend's suggestion, he and his friends planned a weekend trip to Nathia Gali, departing at 7 a.m. on Saturday morning and reaching after a six-hour drive, staying in a hotel room booked through an online application. (2) After resting, they asked locals about tourist spots and were told of a waterfall and a lake nearby, not to be missed; they rented a jeep to the lake, thirty minutes away, and were amazed by pure, clean water coming straight from the mountains, ate fish from there, and sat for an hour enjoying the view. (3) The next day after breakfast they rented a jeep again to see the waterfall; the road was very uneven and dangerous, but the driver was expert and knew the route well; the waterfall was 140 meters high and its sound was like an orchestra's; they took pictures, had tea and ate pakoras from a local stall. Conclusion: It was time for the journey back by bus; the nightlife, the music and the far-stretching hills were alluring them to revisit the place, the zigzag roads gave an opportunity to view nature from different angles, and they would all love to come here again to find out the unexplored spots.

24. Hostel Life
Thesis: Living a hostel life for learning how to study and prepare for classes, to experience different cultures and languages across the country, provides an incredible foundation for students to excel in life, encouraging them to explore and learn, make friends, take responsibility and experience a new sense of independence. Body: (1) The writer travelled from Lahore to Islamabad with his entire luggage to live in a hostel, both excited and sad to leave his family and begin a new chapter; the bus took around 5 hours to the Rawalpindi Terminal, then a taxi to the hostel, surprisingly quite far from the university. (2) The head warden greeted him and shifted him to his allotted room; he was the first to arrive, so setting up his luggage in the cupboards was easy; roommates arrived the next morning, which was orientation day. (3) After the first day at the university, he explored the hostel facilities: the mess hall, gym and a small area designated for Namaz; at first his interaction was limited to roommates, but with each passing day he made new friends, mostly from the computer department while he was from bio sciences, though all shared a common place for daily activities. (4) They were from different cities and shared stories of their experiences; he made lots of good friends, some becoming friends for life. Conclusion: It has been a life-changing experience; he is indebted to the faculty who worked tirelessly to help him and to the opportunities that shaped him; he can proudly say that the time spent at the hostel was the best time of his life and will be a part of him forever.

lessons.title: Essay Outlines — A Visit to a Fair to Smog
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • An essay outline has three parts — Thesis (the main idea), Body (the points in order), Conclusion (the closing thought).
  • Learn the outline point by point, then write the essay in your own words.

Solved Exercises

25. A Visit to a Fair
Thesis: A fair is an annual family-friendly event held in a city or mostly in a countryside; friends from near and far venture on an adventure to spend memorable moments together, entertaining themselves with concerts, great food, animals and adventures, and fairs have a rich history in the Punjab. Body: (1) During the last summer vacation, the writer visited his grandmother's house in Sahiwal with all cousins present; after two days, his uncle announced a fair in the suburb of Sahiwal and took them there the next evening. (2) They reached in time to spend a few hours; a big marquee was divided into portions with different activities; clowns showed spectacular tricks surrounded by kids and laughter. (3) A haunted house, scary with statues, mannequins and skeletons, not allowing kids under five; then animals like horses and goats performing acts, and an aerial performance by acrobats, one girl walking on a rope and a man cycling on a single wheel, which was really scary. (4) Food stalls with traditional food like Qallama, Kulfi and Rabbri; then the well of death, a big well with a car moving in circular motion at around 100 km/hour, giving goosebumps and dizzy heads. Conclusion: The time passed quickly, but that visit to the village fair bestowed a flood of nostalgic memories; it was indeed a memorable trip, and the writer wishes he could visit it again.

26. A Visit to a Historical Place
Thesis: Historical places are very important assets of a country with great significance not only in culture but also in history; historical monuments are the proof of our past and tell us about our lineage and ancestors, and they cannot be separated from a culture because discarding them is like disposing of one's identity. Body: (1) The writer always cherished visiting the Badshahi Masjid, which had been considered the world's largest masjid for almost three centuries, and wanted to see whether all he had heard was true or just exaggeration. (2) He planned a trip with friends on Friday to offer Namaz-e-Jummah there; departing at seven o'clock, they went to the Badshahi Masjid located near the Lahore Fort, now a fine tourist hub with people of different communities gathered there. (3) An elderly person told them the Masjid was constructed between 1671 and 1673 in the reign of Aurangzeb, the famous Mughal Emperor; it was quite spacious, a whole new world inside, with eight minarets and three domes, corridors and lawns, built from red stone with a Persian and Turkish look. (4) It was a trend to build buildings by hiring famous architects from the Persian origin; a spacious room was turned into a museum with old transcripts of the Holy Quran and other Islamic manuscripts; they visited every inch of this Islamic gallery and offered Namaz-e-Jummah there. Conclusion: It was a memorable trip that the writer could never forget.

27. My Hobby
Thesis: Someone has rightly said that a mind with no thoughts is the mind of a demon; an empty mind having no creativity and lacking passion for learning is completely useless in today's world, so nothing can be better than having a hobby to keep free minds occupied and away from worldly worries. Body: (1) People have different hobbies according to their tastes: some like to collect antiques, others like gardening; today's children are more interested in technology, spending free time making videos, watching plays, playing video games and communicating online. (2) For the writer, reading books is what he does in spare time; since childhood he developed a taste for story books, and on his fifth birthday his father gifted him "100 Great Muslim Leaders", which inspired him so greatly that he started purchasing books with his pocket money. (3) The more he grew up, the more he visited different libraries; going to libraries was fruitful and enlightening, and he was amazed that there are so many books on different subjects he had not read, so his passion for books turned into a hobby. (4) Benefits: the more he reads, the more he learns about the world; reading imparts knowledge, guides through different walks of life, gives a feeling of achievement and satisfaction, enhances confidence, fosters appetite for learning, ignites spirit and invigorates in times of despair. Conclusion: This never-ending process of book reading continues and keeps making him read more and more books; this hobby does not let his spark and excitement down in a world full of stress, and book reading is a perfect stress-buster; a person should find a hobby which is interesting and constructive at the same time; his hobby of reading books keeps him indulged and knowledgeable, serving him like an all-weather friend that always stands by his side through thick and thin and never leaves him in the lurch.

28. Women Empowerment
Thesis: The empowerment of women and the improvement of their political, social, economic and health status play an integral part in the development of a country, and it is very important for the achievement of sustainable development; the endeavours of both women and men are highly required for the development of a country. Body: (1) In earlier centuries, women were treated as useless creatures and suffered domestic violence, sexual harassment and physical torture; they could not go out and work like men, and though the scenario has changed gradually, a lot is still left to be desired. (2) In all parts of the world, women are facing threats to their lives, health and well-being as a result of being overburdened with work and their lack of power and influence; in most regions they receive less formal education than men, and their knowledge, abilities and coping mechanisms often go unrecognized. (3) Women empowerment has five components: women's sense of self-worth; their right to have and determine choices; their right to have access to choices; their right to have access to opportunities and resources; and their right to have power to control their own lives, both within and outside the home, and their ability to influence the direction of social change to create a more just social and economic order, nationally and internationally. (4) To bring women into the mainstream of life, proper education is a must; the social right of a human being has to be ensured strictly for women; to implement all the rights of women, laws should be enforced; many working women face problems at workplaces because of gender discrimination and sexual harassment, and authorities should take necessary steps to make their workplaces secure. Conclusion: A nation can't reach its desired goal of development without the help of women; they make more than half of the total population, and if they remain ignorant and unemployed, they can't take part in the development of a country and ultimately become a burden; an empowered woman can stand for her rights with bold decisions, is an asset to a country, and can become a force that gives direction to a society and takes part in economic and political development; if equal rights are ensured to women, they can add new dimensions to the growth of a society.

29. Smog
Thesis: Smog is a type of air pollution which is a mixture of smoke and fog; scientifically, it is a mixture of different pollutants, including oxides of nitrogen (NOx), oxides of sulphur (SOx), carbon monoxide (CO), particulate matter (PM), volatile organic compounds (VOC) and ozone, and the main pollutant responsible for smog build-up is NOx. Body: (1) It describes the atmospheric condition of a particular area; in its worst form it blocks out the winter sunshine, causes closure of motorways after dusk, prevents flights from landing at international airports at night, and residents face a dense blanket of smog that reduces visibility and causes several respiratory and mental ailments. (2) Historically, the most lethal smog was the London Great Smog in 1952, in which more than 12,000 people died from traffic accidents or respiratory ailments; in 2012, Beijing faced deadly smog with a large number of casualties. (3) Over a couple of years, Pakistan and India have been badly hit by smog; in winter, delayed rainfall and cold, continuously dry conditions retain all pollutants in the lower atmosphere, causing smog to spread in both countries.
